title: Turn-based Combat system for my 2.5D RPG
author: irbrandonl
selftext:
Just another little update showcasing some more of GodScar's turn-based combat system!

This time I'm showing off an Ultimate ability, an Ascension ability, and a few different skills.

For anyone curious about the workflow, I'm primarily using Claude Code Opus 5.5 on Extra Effort or Ultracode, with Godot as the game engine and Blender for some of the more complex 3D models. A lot of the process involves giving Claude detailed references, reviewing the results, and going back and forth refining things until they look and function the way I want.

There's still plenty I want to improve, especially with the animations and overall combat presentation, but things are slowly coming together.

As always, I'd love to hear what you guys think! We're still pretty early in development, so any feedback or suggestions are greatly appreciated. Thanks again to everyone who's been following along!

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body:
So one thing, I’ve been commenting on your posts a lot because this is a project I’m super into, but your enemies, one is just a jellyfish, and another is just a pretty big crab.

I can see the charm oozing out of every pore everywhere else in this game, so apply that to the enemies. Make them your own. Nobody wants to fight a normal crab and a normal jellyfish, what can make those enemies your own thing? Think final fantasy with like adamantoise or the coerl. Pretty much a turtle and cheetah right? BUT there is a little special something that makes each of those a unique enemy.

replies.author: irbrandonl
replies.body: I actually really like that idea, thank you! I will say that I have over 100 different monsters in the game, and I've intentionally been showcasing some of the less exciting ones because I don't want to spoil too much. But you've also made me realize that I could do a better job making some of the more basic monster sprites feel unique and stand out. Definitely something I'll be putting more thought into. Great feedback, I appreciate it!
